stories.title: Billionaire Hedge Fund Boss Sues Top Tax KC After HMRC Defeat
In depth: LLPs dodged a bullet in the budget - but HMRC is on their case
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that HMRC is putting professional services firms under aggressive scrutiny following the Supreme Court's BlueCrest ruling on LLP members' self-employment status. Boston Consulting Group's UK arm is reported to be among those targeted, and it says it is in discussion with HMRC. PKF Francis Clark's Andrew Allen warns the tax at stake could be material for law firms, and outlines capital and remuneration steps firms are reviewing.
stories.hook: HMRC is reviewing LLP members' self-employment status after BlueCrest, and PKF Francis Clark warns law firms the tax at stake could be material

stories.title: No costs for solicitor who left LiP in “intolerable position”
stories.ltme_summary: Mr Justice Fordham has refused the London Borough of Tower Hamlets any costs for a judicial review claim after its solicitor, Mr Onuba, served key documents very late on a litigant in person, Mabel Abdul, who is acting for her disabled four-year-old son. The judge said the council had failed to acknowledge its defaults and that the position placed on Ms Abdul was intolerable. The council may not rely on the late documents.
stories.hook: Tower Hamlets loses all costs after judge finds late solicitor documents left a litigant in person in an intolerable position

stories.title: Calls for electronic bills review grow
stories.ltme_summary: The Solicitors Journal reports that Senior Costs Judge Jason Rowley has called for a review of the electronic bill of costs at a roundtable run by the Association of Costs Lawyers. ACL vice-chair Victoria Morrison-Hughes and silk Nick Bacon KC also comment. The ACL says it will help with reform.
stories.hook: Costs judge and Association of Costs Lawyers back review of electronic bill format

stories.title: Legal problems cost businesses time, money
Legal aid system for brain-damaged children deemed unjust
stories.ltme_summary: Lawyers at the Association of Personal Injury Lawyers say Scotland's legal aid rules for families pursuing compensation for brain-damaged children are unjust. Under current rules both parents' finances are assessed. APIL has responded to a Scottish Government consultation on modernising legal aid, arguing that only the child's resources should be considered.
stories.hook: APIL calls Scotland's parental means test for brain-damaged children's legal aid unjust

LSB: Small businesses not getting the legal help they need
stories.ltme_summary: The Legal Services Board says its small business legal needs survey, carried out by YouGov among 10,352 businesses, found that 36 per cent had at least one legal issue in the past year. Only two in ten businesses with a legal need had it met. The survey is the fifth since 2013 and compares with 2021.
stories.hook: LSB survey finds only two in ten small businesses with serious legal needs get help
entities: Office of the Small Business Commissioner

stories.title: A letter from the SRA? Your first reaction matters
stories.ltme_summary: Jonathan Goodwin, a solicitor advocate who has spent decades on professional discipline, writes advice for solicitors who receive an initial letter from the Solicitors Regulation Authority. He says the first response becomes part of the record, that an enquiry is not a verdict, and that solicitors should acknowledge the letter, diarise deadlines, secure documents and seek specialist advice where a matter is serious. The piece is an opinion column.
stories.hook: Jonathan Goodwin says a solicitor's first reply to an SRA letter becomes part of the permanent record

stories.title: Judge seeks new version of electronic costs bill
stories.ltme_summary: Senior Costs Judge Rowley has called for a review of the electronic bill of costs, ten years after its introduction, ahead of the Association of Costs Lawyers Conference. He says the Excel format, which has 55 columns, slows assessment and is hard for litigants in person to follow. He does not favour a return to paper bills, and the Senior Courts Costs Office is looking at the Supreme Court's Form 5 bill as a model.
stories.hook: Senior Costs Judge Rowley wants the 55-column electronic bill of costs reviewed

stories.title: Reorganisation uncertainty continues for council lawyers
stories.ltme_summary: The Law Society Gazette reports that the government will go ahead with local government reorganisation in five areas, while 15 others remain under review. Lawyers in Local Government past president Paul Turner says uncertainty continues for council lawyers. The Ministry of Housing says outcomes for all areas will be known by early next year.
stories.hook: Five councils get reorganisation go-ahead as council lawyers face capacity strain
entities: Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government

stories.title: Solving intake cuts 27% off law firm revenue
stories.ltme_summary: Syntheia, a vendor, argues in a blog post that intake tools for in-house teams could cut law firm revenue.
